title: Charge every read in a regenerative write-and-retry cycle
statement: For exactly-one-event proposals, S=qp/[1-q(1-p)r]. For fixed Poisson pulses with perfect reset/classification and every multi-event pulse terminal, S(x)=qpx exp(-x)/[1-q exp(-x)(1+(1-p)x)]. Its optimum solves1-x-q exp(-x)=0; p=.68,q=.995 gives only.863833 eventual success.

requires: The specified regenerative or fixed-Poisson single-target/no-collateral protocol; identical reset states, perfect classification and failure termination. Illustrative p,q are supplied.
provides: For exactly-one-event proposals, S=qp/[1-q(1-p)r]. For fixed Poisson pulses with perfect reset/classification and every multi-event pulse terminal, S(x)=qpx exp(-x)/[1-q exp(-x)(1+(1-p)x)]. Its optimum solves1-x-q exp(-x)=0; p=.68,q=.995 gives only.863833 eventual success.
assumptions: No measured CrSBr fidelity or physical no-go. Write/read/reset components must hold jointly, and repeated reads do not remove common calibration error.
costs: Charge preparation, calibration/registration, actual incident norm/dose including interference and probe tails, every native-state read, other-species damage, time/energy, all failed/reset/replacement/flip trials and independent replicas. Same-information ordinary microscopy, likelihood, Fourier and retry comparators get the same priors/actions. Full-cycle advantage is UNKNOWN.

body: Zero-event pulses still require paid survival reads. In this supplied model99% success needs read survival>=.999976625, even with perfect reset/classification. Continuous event stopping could change the kernel but needs signal/latency/dose and changed-state evidence. Projected erasure does not supply an exact native-layer reset.
